question: Will Israel or the United States conduct a military strike on Iranian territory between October 29 and October 30, 2026?

calls.reasoning: Status quo: no confirmed US/Israeli strike on Iranian land for weeks; Trump pledged on Oct 8 no attack before the Nov 3 midterms, and Israel prefers to act after its Oct 27 election and then needs to form a coalition. Reference class: since the Apr 8 ceasefire, a few known US strike days on Iranian land (May 7, Jul 15, Sep 1, maybe more) give ~5-10% for a random 2-day window, and the pledge lowers that. Tail risks: Iran attacked ships 26 times in Oct 1-19 vs 13 in all of September, and Netanyahu said on Oct 18 that Israel would strike pre-emptively without US help. Market: no exact match. Polymarket's 'no US strike on Iran by Oct 31' was ~81.5% before a brief, unexplained spike on Oct 19 and 64.5% during it; the Oct 22 contract was ~95.5% before. That implies ~14% for a US strike Oct 23-31; a share of that for these 2 days plus a small chance of Israel acting alone gives ~6%.
calls.dossier:
- Trump said on Oct 8, 2026 that the US will not attack Iran before the Nov 3 midterms; he told Time that strikes are 'possible' after the elections if there is no deal (CBS, Washington Times, Oct 1-9).
- On Oct 19, 2026, Trump warned the US could 'soon finish the job' unless Iran changes course 'rapidly'. He also gave Netanyahu his 'complete and total endorsement' ahead of Israel's Oct 27 election. No date was given (Iran International, Oct 19).
- On Oct 18, 2026, Netanyahu said Israel is ready to strike pre-emptively even without US help, called confronting Iran his life's mission, and named regime change as policy (Arabi21, Oct 18). On Oct 14 he said he does not favor a pre-emptive strike before the Oct 27 election. Israeli sources reportedly told Washington they would prefer any action to begin after the vote.
- Axios (Oct 7, 2026): the Pentagon ordered CENTCOM to be ready for possible Iran strikes while Trump weighs timing. A third carrier (USS Theodore Roosevelt) has been dispatched, with arrival estimated in November.
- JINSA and NBC (Oct 2026): Iran made 26 attacks on ships in Oct 1-19 vs 13 in all of September; 27 of 28 projectiles hit. There has been little US response because of the pre-midterm pledge. Iran mostly uses single drones rather than the fixed coastal launch sites the US struck earlier.
- Known US strikes on Iranian land since the Apr 8 ceasefire: May 7, 2026; Jul 15, 2026 (Greater Tunb Island coastal defenses); Sep 1, 2026 (~100 coastal targets in one day). Not a complete list. No confirmed strike for several weeks as of mid-October.
- Diplomacy: Russia's foreign minister Lavrov was in Tehran on Oct 19 trying to avert a return to large-scale war. Iran's 7-day ceasefire / Hormuz reopening proposal, conditional on lifting the blockade, remains on the table.
- Iran has fortified nuclear sites and is preparing for possible US strikes after the midterms (CNBC, Oct 13).
- Base rate (constructed): about 3+ known US strike days on Iranian land over ~194 days since the ceasefire, so roughly 3-10% of 2-day windows contain a strike, depending on undercount. That is not conditioned on the pre-midterm pledge now in force.
- Resolves off credible reporting of a US or Israeli munition impacting Iranian land territory. Interceptions, strikes at sea and covert sabotage without a munition strike do not count; errant impacts do count.
- Event window: 00:00 UTC Oct 29 -> 23:59 UTC Oct 30, 2026 per the criteria. As of Oct 19, 0% of it has elapsed; it falls after Israel's Oct 27 election and before the US Nov 3 midterms.
- Searched for but not found: any announced date for renewed operations, any confirmed US retaliatory strike in October, and an exact-window betting market. Polymarket only has US-only 'strike by date' contracts (Oct 22, Oct 31, Nov 8, Dec 31).
calls.reference_class: 2-day windows since the Apr 8, 2026 ceasefire containing a US/Israeli strike on Iranian land

calls.reasoning: Base rate: during the blockade phase (Apr 13-Oct 19, ~6 months) US strikes on Iranian land happened in two episodes (Jul 7-30; ~100 coastal targets on Sep 1). That gives roughly 10-15% for a random 2-day window, and lower after about 7 weeks of pause. Status quo is no strikes: Trump publicly pledged no attack before the Nov 3 midterms, and Israel prefers acting after its Oct 27 election, likely coordinated with the US. Upward pressure: Trump's 'finish the job' rhetoric (Oct 18), CNN-reported strike plans for 'before or after' the midterms, Netanyahu saying Israel would strike preemptively without the US, and Iranian ship attacks doubling in October. Market: Polymarket 'no US strike on Iran by Oct 31' fell to 64.5% on Oct 19 after an unexplained spike that partly reversed; it was ~81.5% before. Its Oct 28 contract at 70.5% implies only ~6% for a first US strike in the Oct 29-31 days. That contract covers US strikes only and the whole period to Oct 31, so it is a near-miss, not an anchor.

- Oct 8 2026 (CNN/Axios/CNBC): Trump on Truth Social: 'we will not be attacking Iran at any time prior to the Midterm Elections' (Nov 3); the blockade stays. Media had reported pre-midterm strike planning just before the pledge. His past Iran statements have not always matched his actions.

No US/Israeli strikes on Iranian land reported Sep-mid Oct (CTP Oct 13; Iran International Oct 19; no strikes logged Oct 17-18). Israel and Iran have not traded fire since June.
- Iranian escalation (JINSA): ship attacks were 8 in Aug, 13 in Sep and 26 in Oct 1-19, at least 2 per day, the highest of the war. At least 10 ships hit around Hormuz since Oct 11 (globalsecurity Oct 16). Iran reportedly told Hezbollah a US attack is 'a matter of time'.
- Diplomacy: Iran's FM Araghchi has a 7-day proposal to reopen Hormuz; Lavrov visited Tehran Oct 19 for de-escalation talks; Trump claims 'productive discussions'. Vance (Oct 19) said the US has 'decisively won' in some ways.
- Base rates: two US strike episodes in ~6 months of the blockade phase (about 25 strike days out of ~190, ~13% of days; clustered). Conditional on a public no-strike pledge in force: no strikes in the 11 days since Oct 8.
- Markets: Polymarket has US-only 'strike on Iran by date' contracts (Oct 22/24/28/31/Dec 31) that do NOT match this question: they cover US only, any date up to the deadline, and air/missile strikes. They moved sharply on Oct 19 with no identified trigger and partly reversed. No market found for the exact Oct 29-30 window or for Israeli strikes.
- Searched, not found: any confirmed scheduled operation date; Israeli post-election cabinet timeline; the globalsecurity Oct 17-19 daily updates (paywalled).
calls.reference_class: 2-day windows during the post-April-2026 blockade phase of the US/Israel-Iran war, conditioned on a public US no-strike pledge

calls.reasoning: Status quo: no US/Israeli strike on Iranian land for weeks; Trump publicly pledged (Oct 8) no attack before Nov 3 midterms, and Israel prefers action after its Oct 27 election — the Oct 29-30 window sits inside the US pledge. Upward pressure: Trump's 'soon finish the job' (Oct 18-19), Netanyahu's readiness to strike unilaterally, CENTCOM preparations, Hormuz ship attacks, possible Iranian preemption around Israeli election that would trigger retaliation; any war resuming before Oct 30 would likely include strikes in-window. Polymarket's US-only 'ceasefire continues through' ladder (Oct 19 midday) implied ~29.5% US strike by Oct 28 and ~35.5% by Oct 31 after a noisy, partially reversed 17-pt move; it was ~18.5% for Oct 31 the day before. Not a matching contract (US-only, cumulative); I weight Trump's explicit pledge more heavily than the market does.

- Background: war began Feb 28 2026; 40-day active phase ended in Apr 8 ceasefire; US naval blockade since Apr 13; no Israel-Iran fire since June; no confirmed US/Israeli strike on Iranian land for several weeks as of mid-Oct (globalsecurity daily updates).
- Oct 8 (CNN/WaPo/USNews): Trump on Truth Social: 'We will not be attacking Iran at any time prior to the Midterm Elections... November 3rd', citing 'productive discussions'. Planners are preparing energy/nuclear target options. War unpopular; oil spikes hurt Republicans.
- Oct 13: Trump said the pause 'might be running out in a few weeks'. Pentagon reportedly ordered CENTCOM to finish preparations.
- Oct 14 (Reuters/USNews): Netanyahu does not favor a preemptive strike before the Oct 27 Israeli election; Israel told the US it prefers action to begin after the vote; concerns: postponing the election, home-front toll.
- Oct 17 (ToI): Lapid says Netanyahu can't be trusted not to strike to disrupt the election. Reports/speculation that Iran may strike preemptively around the Israeli election.
- Oct 16 (globalsecurity): at least 10 ships struck in/around Hormuz since Oct 11; CENTCOM blamed Iran for sinking GFS Pride; Trump threatened the Pickaxe Mountain nuclear site; Iran told Hezbollah 'an American attack is a matter of time'; Brent ~$105.80.
- Oct 18-19 (Iran International, Khaleej Times): Trump: unless Iran changes 'rapidly, we will soon finish the job'; endorsed Netanyahu. Netanyahu (Oct 18): Israel ready to strike preemptively without US help; regime change is the objective; '90% of the mission achieved'. Araghchi: 'Be our guest... we have unfinished jobs too'; Iran's 7-day Hormuz reopening proposal still on the table. Lavrov in Tehran Oct 19 for de-escalation talks. VP Vance: US has 'decisively won' in some ways.
- Structural note: if hostilities resume at any point before Oct 30, the Feb-Apr active phase featured near-daily strikes, so in-window strikes would be probable; the question roughly reduces to 'is an active campaign under way on Oct 29-30'.
- Window falls after the Israeli election (Oct 27) but before the US midterms (Nov 3, inside Trump's pledge period); Israeli coalition formation would still be under way.
- Markets: the Polymarket 'US-Iran ceasefire continues through...?' ladder exists (US-only air/missile strike on Iranian territory, cumulative by date; ~$17.6M lifetime volume). It moved sharply on Oct 19 with no identified trigger, and about two-thirds of the drop reversed within 20 min. Not a matching contract (excludes Israel; cumulative rather than a 2-day window).

calls.reference_class: Two-day windows during the 2026 post-ceasefire phase (June-Oct 2026) with no confirmed US/Israeli strikes on Iranian land; conditional on an explicit US presidential no-strike pledge covering the window

calls.reasoning: Status quo: weeks without US/Israeli strikes on Iranian land. The window sits inside Trump's explicit Oct 8 pledge of no attack before the Nov 3 midterms. Israel prefers acting after its Oct 27 election but is coordinating with the US and forming a coalition, so a solo Israeli strike on Oct 29-30 is unlikely (~2-3%). Upward risks: 'finish the job' rhetoric, CENTCOM preparations, Iranian ship attacks doubling in October, Netanyahu's readiness to act unilaterally, and the chance that a campaign started before Oct 29 carries into the window. Polymarket's US-only cumulative ladder implies more (~12-24% when you account for continuation), but it was noisy and spiked; I weight the explicit pre-election pledge more heavily.
calls.reconciliation: No factual conflict: the runs' Polymarket readings agree (Oct 19 spiked state: ~29.5% US strike by Oct 28, ~35.5% by Oct 31; ~18.5% by Oct 31 before the spike). That market is US-only and cumulative, so it is a near-miss. The disagreement is judgment: how much weight goes to Trump's explicit pre-midterm pledge versus a noisy market and escalating rhetoric, and how likely a pre-window strike is to continue into Oct 29-30. Recent US retaliation has been single-day raids, so I discount continuation. I weight the pledge heavily but keep tail risk for retaliation and for an Israeli move after its election. No web access on this run, so nothing was independently verified.

disagreements.verdict: The runs agree once aligned (spiked ~29.5%/35.5%, before the spike ~18.5% for Oct 31). Treated as noisy near-miss evidence.

disagreements.claim: How binding Trump's Oct 8 no-strike-before-midterms pledge is
disagreements.verdict: Mostly binding; I weight it more than the market does, since Iranian ship attacks so far have gone unanswered.

disagreements.claim: Whether a strike before Oct 29 would continue into the window
disagreements.verdict: Partly; recent US actions were one-day raids, so continuation is maybe 50-60%.

disagreements.claim: Probability that Israel strikes alone just after its election
disagreements.verdict: Low (~2-3%): coalition formation and US coordination before the midterms.
